creative_direction: Make a single camellia from three layers of folded paper, viewed nearly from above. The outer petals are warm white, the inner fold is muted crimson, and two small dark green leaves sit behind the bloom. Use a sea-salt blue background with one soft shadow showing the paper thickness. Keep the folds broad and intentional, with visible cut edges and only a few crease lines. The flower should not become a complex origami ball. Center its compact circular silhouette and allow generous empty space around it. No printed pattern, lettering, or additional blossoms. The charm comes from the small differences between the overlapping paper petals and the restrained material depth.
style_inspiration: Original artwork from written art direction; prior conversation informs general design preferences, no prior image pixels reused or uploaded.
